metaDescription: Visit Humayun's Tomb in Delhi: the first great Mughal garden tomb, its history and restoration, the other tombs in the complex, and how to reach it.
description: A visitor's guide to Humayun's Tomb in Delhi: the 16th-century garden tomb of the second Mughal emperor, often seen as a forerunner of the Taj Mahal, the other tombs in the complex including Isa Khan's, the restoration by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture, the site museum, Sunder Nursery next door, practicalities and nearby Nizamuddin.
dek: Humayun's Tomb, set in a quartered garden in Delhi, set the pattern for the great Mughal tombs that followed, including the Taj Mahal.

parent.label: UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India

intro: The Mughal emperor Humayun died in 1556, and his tomb was built in the 1560s and 1570s, commissioned by his widow, Bega Begum, and designed by the Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas. UNESCO describes it as the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent, and it is often seen as a forerunner of the Taj Mahal.

The complex contains many other graves, including those of later Mughals, and earlier monuments such as Isa Khan's tomb. A long restoration led by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture with the ASI brought back its gardens and water channels. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.
quickAnswer: Humayun's Tomb in Delhi is the 16th-century garden tomb of the Mughal emperor Humayun, commissioned by his widow Bega Begum and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993. It is open daily from sunrise to sunset, with ASI tickets available online. Allow two to three hours for the tomb, Isa Khan's tomb and the gardens, and add Sunder Nursery and the Nizamuddin dargah nearby.
takeaways: Built in the 1560s and 1570s; commissioned by Humayun's widow, Bega Begum.
Often seen as the forerunner of the Taj Mahal.
Open daily; tickets from the ASI.
Isa Khan's tomb, the Arab ki Sarai gate and the Nila Gumbad are in the same area.
Sunder Nursery, next door, is a restored Mughal-era garden with more monuments.

items.name: The tomb
body: A red sandstone and white marble mausoleum on a high platform with a double dome, in a charbagh garden divided by water channels.

image.alt: Humayun's Tomb seen across its charbagh garden, Delhi
image.caption: Humayun's Tomb

items.name: Isa Khan's tomb
body: An octagonal tomb of a noble at the court of Sher Shah Suri, built before Humayun's Tomb, just inside the complex.

items.name: The gates and the Arab ki Sarai
body: Gateways and the remains of the enclosure associated with the craftsmen who built the tomb.

items.name: Nila Gumbad and Afsarwala tomb
body: Smaller monuments nearby, including one with blue tiles.

sections.heading: Restoration and the site museum
paras: The Aga Khan Trust for Culture restored the gardens in the early 2000s and then the tomb itself, working with the ASI, using traditional materials and craftsmen. A site museum near the entrance tells the story of the tomb and the Mughal dynasty; check its current opening hours.

sections.heading: Visiting practicalities
list: Open daily from sunrise to sunset; check current hours with the ASI.
Tickets at the gate or online; carry ID.
Allow two to three hours, more with Sunder Nursery.
Early mornings and late afternoons have the best light and fewer visitors.

sections.heading: How to reach
list: Metro: JLN Stadium on the Violet Line is the nearest, a short auto ride away.
Hazrat Nizamuddin railway station is about 2 km away.

items.name: Nizamuddin
body: The dargah of Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya and its qawwali, and the tomb of Ghalib.

items.name: Lodhi Garden
body: Sultanate-era tombs in a large city park.

rows: Humayun's Tomb and Isa Khan's tomb in soft light
Walk through Nizamuddin Basti to the dargah
Return for the qawwali at the dargah

sections.heading: What makes it special
paras: Humayun's Tomb brought together Persian ideas (the double dome, the charbagh garden) with Indian materials and craftsmanship (red sandstone, white marble inlay, small chhatris on the roof). The high platform, the garden aligned on the tomb, and the play of red and white became the language of later Mughal tombs.

safety: Timings, closures and ticket rules are set by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) or the site authority and change from time to time; check the official website before you go, and buy tickets only on official portals.
Do not climb on or touch carvings, and follow the site's rules on photography, drones and tripods.
Weekends and holidays are crowded; arrive at opening time for the calmest visit.
Carry water; the gardens are large and open.
packing: A light shawl for winter mornings
